answer.summary: Feifer said coverage can be valuable as third-party validation even when it brings no immediate response: his company’s Variety story produced no direct results, but he included it in advertiser and partner emails to make recipients pay more attention.

sections.content: Feifer described Money News Network, which he was building with Nicole Lapin. After they worked hard to get Variety to cover their podcast Help Wanted, he said the story brought them “nothing” directly. Still, they included the Variety link in every email to potential advertisers and partners, using the coverage as validation and expecting it to make recipients pay more attention—not as a source of immediate results.
